observation_summary: The type inference engine failed to correctly infer properties of an anonymous object when that object was part of a union type constraint. The compiler expected the object to match the record type, but it failed to propagate the record constraints when the constraint was a union.
reasoning_summary: The fix involves adding logic to iterate through the alternatives of a union type constraint and applying the record type matching logic to any record types found within that union. This is a procedural correction to the type inference algorithm, specifically how it handles constraints, rather than a simple guard (Checking) or a value assignment (Assignment/Initialization).
evidence_used: The fix adds a loop to iterate over union type alternatives in PrototypeObjectType.java.
The bug report describes an inconsistency in type inference when an anonymous object is used in a union.
The failing tests show that the compiler failed to infer the expected record properties.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the fix adds an 'if' condition, the primary purpose is to extend the algorithm's capability to handle union types, not just to validate a parameter.
This is a local procedural fix within the existing type inference logic, not a design-level capability omission.
